reasoning:
POSTCONDITION: a delivered feedback artifact whose items are anchored to timestamps in the learner recording and describe pronunciation differences from the target recording. Acceptance claims the task actually makes: (1) items are timestamped and land where they say; (2) the learner's spoken words are preserved in what is attributed to them; (3) every reported difference is supported by the audio; (4) the supplied dialect notes govern what counts as acceptable in the target variety; (5) the text infers nothing about the speaker's identity, nationality, disability, or effort. No exhaustiveness claim is made ("identify only differences the audio supports" is a precision constraint), so no coverage/recall validator is emitted.

VALIDATOR 1 — prohibited-attribution-check. Failure mode: the artifact attributes origin, L1, identity, a medical/anatomical cause, or effort/emotion to the speaker. Oracle: the delivered artifact's own text — this claim is a property of the text itself and needs no external evidence; the validator reads the file directly. Planted defect ("that trilled /r/ is the classic Spanish-speaker giveaway" or "you rushed this, you weren't concentrating") is caught by quoting the offending file:line. It is required to report the artifact path and total line count so an unread-tail approval is visible.

VALIDATOR 2 — dialect-notes-conformance. Failure mode: the feedback flags as an error a realization the supplied notes license, or asserts a fact about the target variety the notes contradict. Oracle: the supplied dialect notes document, discovered from the task materials and quoted with file:line. Planted defect (an item scolding the learner for a variant the notes list as standard in the target variety) shows up as a direct notes-vs-item contradiction. The validator is explicitly barred from rejecting on its own language knowledge, so notes-silent items cannot become findings.

VALIDATOR 3 — audio-grounded-claim-check. Failure mode: fabricated, mis-timed, or word-altering items. Oracle: the two recordings themselves, seeked at each stated timestamp. Planted defect (an item at 0:14 claiming a devoiced final /d/ in a word that is not spoken there, or a "learner said" quotation that is actually the target form) is caught by listening at that point in both files. Because audio perception cannot be assumed in this runtime, the prompt requires a capability check first and mandates an EVIDENCE GAP with attempted commands rather than a plausibility approval or an unfounded rejection if the audio cannot be obtained — "could not verify" never becomes approval here.

SPLITS AND COUNTERFACTUALS. Timestamp accuracy, word preservation, and difference-support are NOT split: all three are observed by seeking the same instant in the same two files, and one fabricated item fails all three, so merging loses nothing. V1 and V2 are separated from V3 because their evidence is text-only and obtainable even when audio access fails; merging them into V3 would mean an audio evidence gap silently suppresses two checks that are fully provable. V1 and V2 are separated from each other because they consult different authorities (the task's prohibition list vs. the notes document) and need different judgement: spotting hedged personal attribution vs. reasoning over phonological descriptions in a source document. Merged, a validator that finds a notes contradiction would tend to stop there and never audit the tail of the artifact for attribution, and the cheaper attribution scan could not run at level2.

STAGES. Stage 1 holds the two text checks (parallel, no audio, cheap). Stage 2 holds the per-item audio seeking, which is materially more expensive — it loads and inspects two recordings once per item. A prohibited attribution or a notes contradiction is a definite reject, so running the audio pass on such an artifact is pure waste. That is a real cost saving, not a mechanical/evaluative sorting.

FALSE-REJECT AUDIT. A different but compliant artifact passes all three: V1 explicitly permits describing audible speech properties, second-person instructional tone, and statements about the target variety, and only fires when a sentence attributes something to the person; V2 treats notes silence as a non-finding and requires two quotations (item + notes passage) for any rejection, so an artifact covering points the notes never mention approves; V3 rejects only on affirmative hearing, honors the artifact's own timestamp granularity instead of an invented tolerance, treats unresolvable items as unverified rather than defects, and cannot reject for omitted observations, format, ordering, or item count. No validator asks what changed, who acted, or what existed before; none treats a current file as a frozen baseline; none mandates a filename, template, item count, or terminology. The implementation prompt requires no evidence log, transcript, provenance note, or fixed layout — only the deliverable the task asks for, plus a plain statement of the path if the task names no destination, and an honest inability report (which is not completion) if a recording or the notes cannot be accessed.

agents.purpose: Produce timestamped pronunciation feedback on the learner recording against the target recording and the supplied dialect notes.
agents.systemPrompt:
You produce timestamped pronunciation feedback for a learner recording, compared against a target recording, using the supplied dialect notes. You run non-interactively: there is no user to ask, so make your own decisions and proceed.

First, discover your actual inputs and capabilities:
- Locate the learner recording, the target recording, and the dialect notes among the materials supplied with this task. Search the working directory and the task's attachments. Do not assume filenames, and do not assume a file exists until you have found it.
- Determine what you can actually do with audio here: whether you can perceive the recordings directly, and what audio or transcription tooling is genuinely installed. Do not assume ffmpeg, any transcription service, network access, or any other specific tool is available — check.

Then do the work:
- Listen to both recordings, and read what the dialect notes say about the target variety.
- Report differences between the learner's pronunciation and the target, each anchored to a timestamp in the learner recording and to the word or sound it concerns.
- Report only what the audio supports. If you cannot hear a difference clearly, leave it out or state the uncertainty plainly. Do not fill gaps with what learners typically do.
- Preserve the spoken words. Quote the learner's words as actually spoken; do not silently replace them with the target words, a corrected form, or a normalized spelling. If you show a target form for contrast, label it as the target rather than as what the learner said.
- Treat the dialect notes as the authority for what is acceptable in the target variety. Do not flag a realization the notes describe as an accepted variant.
- Describe sounds, not the speaker. Never state or imply the learner's nationality, region of origin, ethnicity, first language, identity, any disability or medical or anatomical condition, or how hard they tried, how careful they were, or how they felt. Hedged versions of these are equally out.
- No placeholders, TODOs, or deferred sections. Finish every part of the feedback you deliver.

Deliver the feedback where the task asks for it. If the task names no destination, save it as a file in the working directory and state the path. Choose a sensible structure yourself; no particular template is required.

If you cannot access or perceive one of the recordings or the dialect notes, say so plainly and describe exactly what you tried. Do not fabricate timestamps, transcriptions, or observations, and do not quietly substitute a different deliverable.

agents.purpose: Verify the delivered feedback infers nothing about the speaker's identity, nationality, disability, or effort.
Verify no flagged difference contradicts the supplied dialect notes.
Verify each timestamped item is present in the audio at the stated time, quotes the learner's actual words, and names a difference the recordings really show.
